title: Personal Credit Cards: autopay source checking account active and not overdrawn on the due date (autopay bank error test)
content:
# Personal Credit Cards: the autopay source checking account on the due date

This rule belongs to the Personal Credit Cards line and reads the cardholder's checking account. When the ground for reversing a late payment fee on a card that carried an automatic payment instruction is decided, the bank error ground requires two facts about the checking account named on the card as the autopay source.

## Rule

1. The autopay source named on the card is a PCB checking account of the cardholder whose status is active.
2. That checking account was not overdrawn on the due date: the date since which it has been negative is empty, or is a date later than the payment due date.
3. The due date examined is the payment due date of the card's most recent statement.
4. A named source that cannot be found as a PCB checking account does not meet the active-status requirement.

Both facts are read from the bank's checking account records for the account named on the card, not from the cardholder's description of it.

## Status check

| Named source account | Meets the active-status requirement |
|---|---|
| PCB checking account of the cardholder, status active | yes |
| PCB checking account in any other status | no |
| no such checking account found | no |

## Overdraft on the due date (hypothetical dates, payment due date 28 June)

| Date since which the checking account has been negative | Overdrawn on the due date |
|---|---|
| empty, the account is not negative | no |
| 29 June, later than the due date | no |
| 28 June, the due date itself | yes |
| 10 June, before the due date | yes |

## Points of judgement

- An account that turned negative the day after the due date was not overdrawn on the due date.
- An account that turned negative on the due date itself was overdrawn on the due date, because that date is not later than the due date.
- An active account that has been negative since before the due date meets the status requirement but not the overdraft requirement.
